task_name: Create nested files and print their tree.
instruction: Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && mkdir -p project/src && touch project/src/main.txt && tree -L 3 project`. Leave the output visible.

task_name: Use sort to order lines alphabetically.
instruction: Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && touch sort_case.txt && echo pear > sort_case.txt && echo apple >> sort_case.txt && echo banana >> sort_case.txt && sort sort_case.txt`. Leave the sorted result visible.

task_name: Archive and extract a text file with zip and unzip.
instruction: Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && echo benchmark > memo.txt && zip memo.zip memo.txt && unzip memo.zip -d out_zip && cat out_zip/memo.txt`. Leave the final output visible.
Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && echo tarcheck > tar_note.txt && tar -cf packed.tar tar_note.txt && ls`. Keep the output visible.

task_name: Create a file and verify it appears in du output.
instruction: Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && echo usage-check > usage_check.txt && du -a .`. Leave the output visible.

task_name: Collect identity and kernel info into a note file.
instruction: Open Terminal, run `cd ~/Documents && id > sysinfo.txt && uname -a >> sysinfo.txt && cat sysinfo.txt`, and leave the output visible.

task_name: Resolve and compare script paths with two commands.
instruction: Open Terminal, run `whereis ~/Scripts/fizzbuzz.sh > path_check.txt && which ~/Scripts/fizzbuzz.sh >> path_check.txt && cat path_check.txt`, and leave the result visible.

task_name: Create and sort a three-line note in Terminal.
instruction: Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && echo alpha > notes.txt && echo beta >> notes.txt && echo gamma >> notes.txt && sort -r notes.txt > notes_sorted.txt && cat notes_sorted.txt`. Leave the sorted output visible.

task_name: Create and verify a phrase file in Terminal.
instruction: Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && echo terminal benchmark pass > phrase.txt && cat phrase.txt`. Leave the output visible.

task_name: Create a file in Terminal and copy its content into Text Editor.
instruction: Open Terminal and run `cd ~/Documents && echo sync-check > sync_note.txt && cat sync_note.txt`. Then open Text Editor and type exactly `sync-check`.
